Prevention: Prevention particulaly important as difficult to contol.
Seeds considered unimportant; tubers are the main means of spread
Clean tools and farm machinery to prevent tubers being spread
Use of deep tillage (>12cm) to destroy tubers and rhizomes in the soil by dessication (most effective in dry soil) or exhausting food reserves
Control established populations near waterways to prevent spread during flooding and storm events
Monitoring: Erect, perennial sedge (30-60 cm high), with extensive underground network of tubers.
Tubers dark brown/black, irregular shaped, 1-2 cm long at maturity, with several buds.
Leaves linear with distinct midrib, 7 mm wide.
Inflorescence with several unequal 'branches', each 2-6 cm long, emerging from the tip of the stem; each with 3-8 purplish-brown flowerheads.
Regularly inspect fields, in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when found
Look out for it in wetlands and along waterways; water and storm events can spread tubers
Direct Control: Hand-weeding at least 2 times until crop canopy formed: the weed is shade intolerant
Pyroxsulam (45%) at 500 mL/ha to suppress weeds
Glyphosate (48%) at 4L/ha applied on actively growing weeds before sowing controls the weed effectively
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
